advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Limit the no-code-read degrade to PASS verdicts (or keep the agent's findings and mark the run as answered, not as an outage) instead of sending every agentic verdict through the outage path
evidence: src/rebar/llm/workflow/gate_dispatch.py:249: `# An agent that read no code cannot certify a PASS (bug bridal-gifted-vampirebat).`

src/rebar/llm/workflow/gate_dispatch.py:250-254: `unread = ... agentic_unread_error(rec) if engine == "agentic" else None` / `if unread is not None: return _plan_review_recovery._degraded_plan_review_verdict(...)`: the verdict's value (PASS/FAIL) is never checked.
src/rebar/llm/workflow/plan_review_recovery.py:486-504: the degraded verdict re-runs only `det_floor` and partitions `det_blocks, det_advisories, []`, so the agent's findings are lost.

src/rebar/llm/workflow/plan_review_recovery.py:494: `"llm_ran": False` and :505-506 `NO provider_provenance ... no provider answered at all`. Both are false for an agent that answered without reading code.
advisory.finding: The no-code-read check replaces every successful agentic verdict, including FAIL verdicts that carry agent findings, with the generic outage INDETERMINATE. That verdict keeps only DET findings and records `llm_ran: False` even though a provider answered. The agent's own findings and `provider_provenance` are silently dropped, though the comment and the commit say the goal is only to stop a PASS from being certified.
scenarios: The agent spots a plan-only defect (e.g. missing acceptance criteria) without opening a file and returns FAIL with a blocking finding. The operator gets an INDETERMINATE saying the LLM did not run, with the finding gone and the resolution_class FIX_AGENT_DESIGN.
Telemetry and coverage consumers that key on `llm_ran`/`llm_unavailable` count this as an outage instead of an agent that answered without reading code.
advisory.suggested_fix: Gate on the verdict value, e.g. `if engine == "agentic" and verdict.get("verdict") == "PASS"`, before calling `agentic_unread_error`. Or build a dedicated INDETERMINATE that keeps the agent's findings and provenance and sets `llm_ran: True`, rather than reusing `_degraded_plan_review_verdict`.

src/rebar/llm/workflow/gate_dispatch.py:250-254: the unread check returns _degraded_plan_review_verdict before the verdict is inspected
ADR 0123 addition: "An agentic run that read no code ... also resolves INDETERMINATE and is never signed"
advisory.finding: Every unread-run case uses an agent with no findings, so the tests only show that a would-be PASS is downgraded. The new check in gate_dispatch runs before any verdict-type branch, so it also turns a would-be BLOCK into INDETERMINATE, dropping the blocking findings. No test pins that outcome, even though ADR 0123 states it for any agentic run that read no code.
scenarios: _UsageFake({"requests": 1, "tool_calls": 0, "distinct_fetches": []}, findings=[_f("F1", "blocker")]) should give INDETERMINATE per the ADR, but no test covers it, so a later change that lets BLOCK through (or vice versa) would not be caught.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add a test: v = _review(repo, tid, _UsageFake({"requests": 1, "tool_calls": 0, "distinct_fetches": []}, findings=[_f("F1", "blocker")])); assert v["verdict"] == "INDETERMINATE"; assert v["coverage"]["resolution_class"] == "FIX_AGENT_DESIGN"

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Base the 'read code' check on tool calls that succeeded (e.g. a read_file whose return was not an error), not on the arguments the model passed
evidence: plan_review_recovery.py:458: `if not isinstance(usage, dict) or not usage or usage.get("distinct_fetches"):` then `return None` (no degrade, so the verdict is signed)

usage_log.py:197-203: for every ToolCallPart, `target = fetch_target(name, getattr(part, "args", None))`, and `if target is not None:` the call is appended to distinct_fetches. This is built from the model's tool-call parts, not from tool results.
usage_log.py:302-321: fetch_target returns the `path`/`query` argument string for read_file/search_files/list_directory without checking that the path exists or that the tool returned content
Absence: plan_review_recovery.py has no check of tool-return parts (success or error) before treating the run as having read code
plan_review_recovery.py:458: `if not isinstance(usage, dict) or not usage or ...: return None`, where `not usage` exempts `{}`
structured_run.py:507-517: `_extract_usage` has `except Exception: ... return {}`
runner_support.py:156-162: `_merge_success_run_shape` has `except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 — telemetry must never break the call path` and only logs a warning
runner.py:698: `result["_usage"] = usage`, so the real runner reports the same `{}` an offline fake does
gate_dispatch.py:250-256: when `unread is None`, the verdict is returned and goes on to be signed; `runner_sel.name` is in scope but isn't used to limit the exemption to the fake runner
tests/unit/test_plan_review_agentic_verdict.py: `test_a_runner_that_reports_no_usage_is_unchanged` with `ids=["absent", "empty"]` locks in `{}` → signed PASS
advisory.finding: The code-read check counts attempted fetch calls, not successful reads. An agent that calls read_file on a path that doesn't exist (or runs search_files with no matches, or lists '.') still gets a non-empty `distinct_fetches`, so a review that actually read no code can still be signed PASS.
merged_from: On the real PydanticAIRunner, if both best-effort telemetry steps fail (`_extract_usage` returns `{}` and `_merge_success_run_shape` swallows its exception), `_usage` ends up as an empty dict. The check treats an empty dict as 'runner reported no usage (offline fake)' and returns None, so the review is signed without any proof the agent read code. The exemption is decided by the shape of the data rather than by runner identity.
scenarios: The frontier model makes up a file path, read_file returns an error string, the model answers with no findings, and the agentic verdict is PASS and gets signed
A single `list_directory('.')` or `search_files` with zero matches satisfies the check
